summary: Specifies 16 additional optional system administration operations for IPP 1.1, with a few associated attributes, values, and status codes. It also uses the IPP Printer object to manage printer fan-out and fan-in.

eli5.summary: A set of extra buttons for the person who looks after the printers, like pause, restart, and turn off.

subtitle: Sixteen optional operator commands for IPP printers, from pausing and holding to reordering jobs, plus a way to chain printers into trees.

tldr.problem: IPP/1.1 focuses on end users and has only a few administrative operations, so operators had no standard way to enable, disable, restart or shut down a Printer, or to suspend, promote and reschedule jobs.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3998 defines 16 additional OPTIONAL operations (10 on the Printer, 6 on jobs), a few new attributes, state-reason values and one status code, and lets a Printer object act as the parent of other Printer objects (fan-out and fan-in).
tldr.outcome: Because every operation is optional, an IPP Printer can support any combination that respects the pairing rules, and it must require TLS client authentication and operator authorization to run them.

today: RFC 3998 is a Proposed Standard from March 2005, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on IPP/1.1 as defined in RFC 2911.

sections.title: Introduction and Terminology
sections.content:
The Internet Printing Protocol (IPP) version 1.1 (RFC 2911 and RFC 2910) concentrates on what end users need, with only a few administrative operations. RFC 3998 adds more OPTIONAL operations for end users, operators and administrators to control Jobs and Printers. The requirements and use cases behind it are in RFC 3239.

It also extends the Printer object so that Printers can be arranged in trees and inverted trees (Fan-Out and Fan-In). A Subordinate Printer is controlled by another Printer; a Leaf Printer has none; a Non-Leaf Printer (also called a Parent Printer) has one or more; a Chained Printer is a Non-Leaf Printer with exactly one. An Output Device is the physical imaging mechanism a Printer controls.
sections.eli5: IPP already lets people send print jobs. This document adds controls for the person in charge of the printers, and a way for one printer to boss around other printers.

sections.title: The Printer Operations
sections.content:
Ten operations target a Printer object, and the client MUST always supply the printer-uri operation attribute. All are OPTIONAL, and many come in pairs where both are REQUIRED if either is implemented. Each needs the authenticated user to be an operator or administrator of the Printer.

Input versus output of jobs. Disable-Printer makes the Printer reject Job Creation operations (Print-Job, Print-URI, Create-Job) with server-error-not-accepting-jobs by setting printer-is-accepting-jobs to false, while queries, Send-Document and Send-URI still work and existing jobs continue. Enable-Printer reverses it. Pause-Printer-After-Current-Job independently controls the output side: the Printer MUST finish sending the job it is sending, MUST NOT send more jobs to its Output Devices or Subordinate Printers, and ends in the stopped state with the paused reason, passing through moving-to-paused if finishing takes appreciable time.

Holding and deactivating. Hold-New-Jobs lets all current pending and processing jobs finish, but puts every newly created job into pending-held with job-held-on-create and adds hold-new-jobs to printer-state-reasons; Release-Held-New-Jobs undoes it. Deactivate-Printer performs a Disable-Printer and a Pause-Printer-After-Current-Job, then rejects everything except Activate-Printer, queries, Send-Document and Send-URI, and sets the deactivated reason. Activate-Printer reverses this.

Restart and shutdown. Restart-Printer is a software re-boot for a Printer behaving erratically: it MUST try to save job and Printer information, returns the Printer to idle, clears the state reasons and sets printer-is-accepting-jobs to true. Because it can be drastic, the client SHOULD try Deactivate-Printer first. Shutdown-Printer adds the shutdown reason, performs a Deactivate, and the Printer object eventually disappears; only Startup-Printer, for hosted implementations, can start a new instance, which comes up idle and not accepting jobs.
sections.eli5: Some buttons stop new papers coming in, some stop papers going out to the printer, and some do both. The restart button is like turning a computer off and on again, and the shutdown button turns the printer off until someone starts it up again.

sections.title: The Job Operations
sections.content:
Six operations target a Job object, identified by a single Job URI or by a Printer URI plus a Job ID; implementations MUST support both forms.

  • Reprocess-Job creates a new job as a copy of a completed, canceled or aborted job retained in the queue, with a new job-uri and job-id and progress counters reset to 0. The original is unchanged.
  • Cancel-Current-Job cancels the job that is currently processing. On a shared printer the current job can change between the request and its acceptance, so a client MAY supply job-id; if that job is not the current one the Printer MUST reject the request with client-error-not-possible.
  • Suspend-Current-Job moves the current job to processing-stopped with the job-suspended reason so other jobs can run, and Resume-Job returns it to pending. If either is supported, both MUST be.
  • Promote-Job makes a pending job the next one processed after the current job, and sets job-priority to the highest supported value if that attribute is implemented.
  • Schedule-Job-After places the target job immediately after a predecessor job named by predecessor-job-id. The RFC's example: with a queue of A, B, C, D, E, scheduling E after B gives A, B, E, C, D. Without a predecessor it behaves like Promote-Job.

Suspend and Resume are different from Hold-Job and Release-Job, which hold and release held jobs rather than suspend running ones. Job operations may be performed by the job owner (Cancel-Current-Job, Suspend-Current-Job, Resume-Job) or by an operator or administrator; the scheduling operations are for operators and administrators.
sections.eli5: These buttons work on one print job at a time: cancel the one printing right now, pause it so another can go first, make a job next in line, or put a job right behind a chosen one.

sections.title: New Status Code, Attributes and Values
sections.content:
The RFC adds a handful of protocol elements. The new status code is server-error-printer-is-deactivated (0x050A), for a Printer deactivated by Deactivate-Printer that only accepts Activate-Printer and query operations.

Two new Printer Description attributes, subordinate-printers-supported and parent-printers-supported (both a set of URIs), record the fan-out relationships. New printer-state-reasons values are hold-new-jobs and deactivated, and the new job-state-reasons value is job-suspended.

Most operations accept the printer-message-from-operator or job-message-from-operator operation attribute (defined in RFC 3380) so operators can record why they acted. It is OPTIONAL for the Printer to support, and ignored if unsupported. Operations on jobs may also carry job-id and job-uri as shown in the RFC's tables.
sections.eli5: The new buttons come with new labels and notes: a status message for the deactivated state, a way to leave a note saying why you pressed a button, and fields that show which printers are the parents and children.

sections.title: Printer Fan-Out and Fan-In
sections.content:
IPP/1.1 let one Printer object represent several Output Devices, but clients could not see or control the individual devices. RFC 3998 generalizes this: a Non-Leaf Printer submits jobs to its immediate Subordinate Printers, which can themselves have subordinates. In Fan-Out one Printer sits above several; in Fan-In several Non-Leaf Printers share one Subordinate Printer. A Non-Leaf Printer MUST NOT have an associated Output Device; Leaf Printers do, and it is RECOMMENDED that each Leaf has only one.

A Subordinate Printer MUST still be a conforming Printer. Its URI can use the parent's host, so every operation passes through the parent, or a different host, in which case the parent MAY track state by polling or by event subscription (RFC 3995).

Forwarding rules. A Non-Leaf Printer MUST NOT forward Printer operations such as Enable-Printer, Disable-Printer or Restart-Printer to its subordinates; a client that wants a subordinate targets its URI directly. By contrast, operations that affect jobs, including job creation, Reprocess-Job, Resume-Job, Promote-Job and Cancel-Job, MUST be forwarded, except Cancel-Current-Job, which MUST NOT be forwarded. Forwarding is on a best-efforts basis: the Printer replies without waiting for its subordinates, so a forwarded request could fail.

The RFC also describes original-requesting-user-name, which keeps the first user's name, while requesting-user-name is updated at each hop. When reconfiguring a tree, the operator SHOULD first deactivate the Printers involved, update the pointer attributes, then reactivate them.
sections.eli5: One print boss can have several helper printers under it, like a teacher passing work to different groups. Orders about a single job get passed down, but orders about the boss printer itself stay with the boss.

sections.title: Conformance Dependencies
sections.content:
All operations are OPTIONAL, but support for some requires others. Enable-Printer and Disable-Printer must come together, as must Hold-New-Jobs with Release-Held-New-Jobs, and Suspend-Current-Job with Resume-Job. If Pause-Printer or Pause-Printer-After-Current-Job is supported, Resume-Printer MUST be too. Activate-Printer requires Deactivate-Printer and vice versa, and Schedule-Job-After requires Promote-Job.

Restart-Printer, Shutdown-Printer, Startup-Printer, Reprocess-Job, Cancel-Current-Job and Promote-Job have no dependencies. Matching state reasons are REQUIRED too: paused for the pause and deactivate operations, hold-new-jobs for Hold-New-Jobs, deactivated for Deactivate-Printer and job-suspended for Suspend-Current-Job.
sections.eli5: Some buttons only make sense in pairs, like on and off. If a printer has one of the pair, it has to have the other.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The Printer operations in this RFC are meant for operators and administrators, and the job operations for the job owner, operator or administrator. Since these operations affect service for all users, misuse by an unauthenticated end user can degrade service for everyone.

Therefore IPP Printers MUST support both successful certificate-based TLS client authentication and successful operator or administrator authorization to perform them. How an operator or administrator is authorized is outside the scope of this RFC. The RFC states that TLS with client authentication addresses the Denial of Service, Man in the Middle and Masquerading threats. It says its internationalization considerations are the same as those of RFC 2911.
sections.eli5: Because these buttons can stop the printer for everybody, only a proven operator is allowed to press them, using a secure connection and a proper ID check.

items.label: Enable-Printer
items.desc: Allows the Printer to accept Job Creation operations.

items.label: Disable-Printer
items.desc: Prevents the Printer from accepting Job Creation operations.

items.label: Pause-Printer-After-Current-Job
items.desc: Pauses the Printer after the current job has been sent to the Output Device.

items.label: Hold-New-Jobs
items.desc: Finishes pending jobs; new jobs go to pending-held.

items.label: Release-Held-New-Jobs
items.desc: Releases held jobs and stops holding new ones.

items.label: Deactivate-Printer
items.desc: Puts the Printer into a read-only deactivated state.

items.label: Activate-Printer
items.desc: Restores the Printer to normal activity.

items.label: Restart-Printer
items.desc: Restarts the Printer and re-initializes the software.

items.label: Shutdown-Printer
items.desc: Shuts the Printer down so it cannot be restarted or queried.

items.label: Startup-Printer
items.desc: Starts up the instance of the Printer object.

cells: OPTIONAL: successful-ok; later becomes stopped with paused
REQUIRED: successful-ok (not in the middle of sending a job)

items.label: Reprocess-Job
items.desc: Creates a copy of a completed job with a new Job ID and processes it.

items.label: Cancel-Current-Job
items.desc: Cancels the current job on the Printer, or the named job if it is current.

items.label: Suspend-Current-Job
items.desc: Suspends the current job so other jobs can be processed.

items.label: Promote-Job
items.desc: Makes the pending target job next after the current job(s).

items.label: Schedule-Job-After
items.desc: Schedules the target job immediately after a specified job.
